B.reason: crab: PE general name for crabs.
handle: PE handle of bucket, basket; Andrews 1865 has the calabash-hanging strings.
split: PE spells it mahae, to tear, split (PPN masae).
bunch: PE bunch or cluster; Andrews 1865.
pond: Andrews 1865 standing water, puddle; PE writes kiʻo wai, pool of water.
spikes: PE thorn, barb, spine; Andrews 1865 having many sharp points.
rake: PE kope 1 rake (PPN tope), distinct from the loans coffee and copy.
staff: PE spells it koʻokoʻo, cane, staff (PPN tokotoko).
forked stick: PE Y-shaped crosspiece, Y-shaped branches; Andrews 1865.
eye: PE spells it ʻōnohi, eyeball; Andrews 1836 and 1865.
flag: PE flag, banner, from hae 'torn' kapa; Andrews 1865 calls the flag sense modern but it is in the 1830s Bible.
load: PE burden carried on the back.
fill: PE full, filled (verb 'to fill' is hoʻopiha); close enough.
fields: PE garden, cultivated field (PPN maʻala).
banner: PE flag, tapa on a stick marking kapu (PCP lepa).
carrier: PE carrying net for calabashes (PCP tootoo).
peaks: PE summit, peak; Andrews 1865 top of a mountain.
fan: PE spells it peʻahi, fan; Andrews 1865.
fin: PE fins between gill plate and ventral fin (pectoral fin).
carry: PE carry on the shoulders.
roots: PE tap root, main root.
fork: PE mana 2 branch, crotch, road fork (PPN manga).
pupil: PE ʻōnohi eyeball, center; Andrews 1865 center of the eye, apple of the eye.
breasts: PE milk, wet nurse, breast.
